page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-200s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring a memory-optimized configuration. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware includes 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark results show a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top tier (top 10%) and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is more limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the average and bottom 25% categories respectively. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, while small-block cached read bandwidth is weak.

The server exhibits performance bottlenecks in highly concurrent or database-heavy tasks, as evidenced by poor results in Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput. Similarly, LLM inference speeds for medium models are poor. However, the high memory allocation per core and strong single-threaded performance make this instance qualitatively cost-effective for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallelization. Suitable workloads include single-threaded data processing, text processing, caching layers, and lightweight memory-bound applications.
description: The Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-200s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server designed for memory-intensive workloads. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 200 GB NVMe SSD. While single-core performance is strong—ranking in the top tier for stress-ng single-core benchmarks—multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth are more modest, with multi-core Geekbench scores and database operations falling into the lower percentiles. This hardware profile offers a qualitatively cost-effective solution for memory-bound tasks that do not require high parallel processing power. It is best suited for single-threaded data processing, text processing, caching, and lightweight memory-optimized applications.
